cells.tense: Right now the two claims on you are held evenly, and neither one is being dropped.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Cook the meal you're known for and hand the recipe to whoever eats it, naming where each thing came from. That evening, at the table.
cells.core:
Two claims land on the same week and you keep both lit without dropping either. No side gets chosen, nothing gets announced; you tend what sits nearby until the scales come level, and the people living on the fair side don't learn there was a choice to make.

This week do the work where it can be seen. Cook the meal you're known for and hand the recipe to whoever eats it, naming where each thing came from. You've kept this out of sight long enough — let the table watch it happen once. What gets handed over in the open stays handed over, and the next time two claims arrive you'll set them level with less weight on you.
cells.sheetLine: Two claims held even, and nobody hears you holding them.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: where what is owed is weighed and set right

cells.tense: Soon the future is being supplied for a season past what anyone asked, and the ground under it is left untended.
cells.act: savour the realised thing without reaching past it
cells.ask: Eat one meal you cooked with the phone off and nothing running underneath. Sit down to it. Stop when the plate is empty.
cells.core:
You get ahead of what the growing thing will need and you're already three seasons out. From where you stand that's care, and it's honest care. What's happening is that providing has become the point, and holding still reads as hands that have quit. So the future gets laid in like a supply, and something close to you is fed on a schedule it didn't set. That's the bill for bracing.

Tonight, eat one meal you cooked with the phone off and nothing running underneath. Sit down to it. One plate, no list, and stop when the plate is empty. Tending that doesn't pause can't tell what's actually there to tend. If you let the meal be finished, you'll feel where the work lands and where you've been supplying a season nobody is in.
cells.sheetLine: You're providing for a season nobody asked you for.

cells.tense: The two claims stopped being weighed some while back, and you are not the one sorting them now.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Water the plants you let go dry. Or do the task that used to need no asking. Today only, and nothing after it.
cells.core:
Two things want holding at once and that work isn't in your hands anymore. The kitchen waits, the decision waits, the correcting happens somewhere else, and whoever notices first keeps the ground up. What you were known for went quiet, and nothing in you has asked for it back. That's where you stand.

Water the plants you let go dry. Or do the task that used to need no asking. Today only, and nothing after it — that last part holds the whole thing. A garden doesn't come back at once; it comes back underneath, one honest watering at a time. You'll feel the point first and the pull toward more later, and either is fine.
cells.sheetLine: The care is still there. Nothing in you has asked for it back.

cells.tense: You keep the two claims even, everyone drinks from it, and you still file that under practical.
cells.act: let what you gave up be seen by the people it was for, without a word about it
cells.ask: When someone is better off from a choice you made, don't say it was nothing. Let it stand a second. One word, then drop it.
cells.core:
Two demands get held level and you file the whole thing under practical. Nobody is told what was set aside to keep it level, and the quiet hands stay quiet. That evenness is a holding in place of something surrendered early. From outside it reads as having no preference at all.

Next time someone is better off from a choice you made, don't wave it off as nothing. Leave the fact standing a second longer before you turn the subject. One word, no speech, then drop it. What you set down gets its place out where it can be seen, and the scale you carry loses a weight you didn't choose.
cells.sheetLine: Filed as practical. Nobody hears what it cost.
